newsitem.title: HONG KONG: MTRC looks at ways to advance airport rail opening.
newsitem.headline: MTRC looks at ways to advance airport rail opening.

text.p: Mass Transit Railway Corp. (MTRC) said on Wednesday it was looking at ways of opening its airport railway at the same time that Hong Kong's new airport opens for business in April 1998.
The rail line from Chek Lap Kok airport to downtown Hong Kong is currently set to open two months after the airport.

"We are of course -- and have been for a long time -- aware of the importance of having the railway available at the same date as the airport," MTRC projects director Russell J. Black said in a news conference.
He said MTRC would discuss the matter with contractors.
"We would have to discuss with the contractors the acceleration of the programme, (how to) take two months out of the programme," Black said.
But little could be done to speed things up until heavy civil engineering work still under way is completed, he said.
However, tracklaying, the most critical part of the railway programme, was on schedule, he said.

The 34-kilometre HK$35.1 billion railway will provide railway services between Hong Kong island and the new airport via the Kowloon peninsula, Tsing Yi island and Lantau island. The airport will cost HK$70.7 billion.
